fields.site.title: Magan Himanshu — Materials Science Research
fields.site.description: Magan Himanshu is a doctoral researcher at Université Paris-Saclay working on high-entropy oxides, functional nanomaterials, and photoelectrochemistry.
fields.hero.name:
Magan
Himanshu
fields.hero.intro: Exploring how composition, crystal structure, and nanoscale processing shape the behaviour of functional materials.

fields.about.heading:
What connects a material’s
structure to its function?
fields.about.paragraph1: I am a materials science researcher with a background in physics. My doctoral research at Université Paris-Saclay explores the design and development of functional materials for energy and environmental applications.
fields.about.paragraph2: I am interested in understanding how composition and processing influence a material’s properties, and using these relationships to guide the development of materials for practical applications.
fields.research.heading:
From complex compositions
to functional materials.
fields.research.intro: Three connected strands of my research, from current doctoral work to earlier nanomaterials studies.
fields.research.1.label: DOCTORAL RESEARCH
fields.research.1.title:
High-entropy
oxides & tungstates
fields.research.1.description: Investigating multication oxides and wolframite-type tungstates, with mono- and bimetallic compositions as references for understanding structural and optical behaviour.
fields.research.2.label: ENERGY CONVERSION
fields.research.2.title:
Electrochemistry &
photoelectrochemistry
fields.research.2.description: Studying oxide electrodes for water-splitting applications, connecting electrochemical response and light-driven behaviour with composition and material processing.
fields.research.3.label: FUNCTIONAL NANOMATERIALS
fields.research.3.title:
Nanomaterials &
sustainable synthesis
fields.research.3.description: Earlier research on biomass-assisted synthesis, transition-metal nanohybrids, and photocatalytic degradation, alongside collaborative work on liquid-crystal nanocomposites.
